text:
Vegas arrives in Columbus after a 6-2 loss at STL two days ago, its second straight by that score, though Aleksanteri Kaskimaki picked up his first NHL point. The Golden Knights are 3-2-0 in their last five and are without Mitch Marner, who had twelve points in eleven games. Alexander Holtz has taken his spot beside Karlsson and Howden, and Ivan Barbashev is up to 18:52 a night from 15:52. Columbus is 1-4-0 in its last five after a 6-2 loss to TOR, where Marshall Rifai scored his first NHL goal. The Blue Jackets are better than their record: their 46% share of expected goals (the quality of chances) says finishing, not play, has cost them.

At five on five there is little between them: VGK has 53% of the expected goals in its games, CBJ 49%. The matchup to watch is special teams, since VGK's power play creates 0.82 expected goals a game and CBJ's penalty kill allows 0.89, and Columbus takes 4.2 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Carter Hart (VGK) and Cam Talbot (CBJ) are both below expectation this season, at -1.1 and -0.9 goals saved above expected. Last season Talbot was at -13.7 over 34 games, Hart -4.4 over 18.

Jack Eichel is 76% for a point, and Mark Stone is 36% to score. Adam Fantilli, the No. 3 pick in 2023, is 27% to score and 55% for a point. Among our under-the-radar picks, Trevor Connelly (VGK) has 2.3 expected goals in his last 10 games from third-line minutes, and we have him at 21% to score. We also like Fantilli's chances for a point, since his line creates 3.96 expected goals per 60 with him on the ice.
